gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Noto Sans Thai Looped has lowercase bodies so large they look bold, with wide gaps at the curve ends. Noto Sans Thai Looped feels clean beside Nordic, whose single stroke weight and scattered spacing read ancient.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Ancient force up top, crisp modern text below. Nordic is strongest where strokes join without thinning, while Noto Sans Tirhuta excels at a dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave big gaps.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-yi: A constant-width outline you can trace with a finger gives Nordic its ancient force. Noto Sans Yi works with a deep lowercase midsection and rounds left unsealed, like an unlatched hook, to keep the page moving.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-oxygen: Oxygen flows easily, its curves never closing back on themselves. Over pages of text its lowercase, nearly matching the capitals, would keep a steady contemporary pace, with Nordic's closed brush-dab letters as the ancient counterpoint.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-pt-sans-caption: Ancient muscle, then a friendlier line: PT Sans Caption has big-bodied lowercase and bowls left unclosed and inviting. Nordic's unshaded, constant strokes carry the display voice while the body keeps quiet.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-questrial: Ancient weight up front, then a flat, stencil-cut line of single-weight strokes. Questrial leaves its curves open, a welcome release from the cramped, pressed-leaf openings in Nordic's letters.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-radio-canada-big: Contemporary in feel, Radio Canada Big finishes terminals well away from the stem and lets its x-height fill the line. And Nordic earns its keep big and short, where its closed letters can command attention.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro opens its terminals broadly and keeps a tiny gap between lowercase and caps. And over paragraphs of text, its unvarying weight from word to word should keep the eye moving.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-saira: Cramped and ancient on top, crisp and clear below. What stands out most is the closed-versus-open split: Nordic seals its letters while Saira leaves a see-through gap in each s and lets rounds climb toward the top line.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk gives its e and a generous open bowls and never lets a terminal close in. Schibsted Grotesk would take over if Nordic were made small, because closed letters lose their punch.
